blocks.t: Evolve product development with expanded patterns and unified accessibility standards
Get the latest on integrated accessibility requirements, refreshed data visualization guidance, updated patterns, and more.

The Visa Product Design System (VPDS) continues to evolve with updates that strengthen our hub for designers and developers. From code library updates to a more unified accessibility experience, these improvements make it easier to build clear, consistent, and inclusive products across Visa.

This release introduces integrated Global accessibility requirements and refreshed charts guidance— making it easier than ever to find, understand, and apply the standards that shape high‑quality product experiences. Our engineering teams have also delivered a series of refinements across the Nova libraries, included expanded pattern examples, dark mode for improved usability in low‑light environments, and enhanced metadata to support agent‑assisted workflows.
Dive into the rest of the updates below.

Check out the latest refinements and updates from our engineering and development teams. Explore the Angular, Flutter, React, and Styles (CSS) changelogs for more information on library-specific updates.

Work faster with new examples for dynamic table, chat, and file upload, available in both Nova Angular and Nova React. Each pattern is available alongside robust usage and accessibility guidance, ensuring designers and developers are empowered to create consistent experiences.

Switch seamlessly between light and dark modes in the site’s top navigation. Designed for clarity in low‑light environments, this update also introduces improved color, date, and time inputs—helping you work comfortably and confidently in whichever mode you prefer.

Experience clearer agent orientation and improved results from AI tools with enhanced metadata updates across Nova assets. These updates include copy markdown buttons on all site pages, updates to llms.txt, and additional metadata to improve agent readability.
